host_load: 1-minute load average 0.00 to 0.15 when each lane attempt began (before any wait for the instance to be ready)

lanes.name: Lambda, warm
lanes.start: HTTPS GET to the function URL, environment already running
lanes.config: provided.al2023, arm64, 2048 MB, function URL with IAM auth, BOOT_RACE_EXIT_AFTER_RESPONSE=0
lanes.check: 30 samples answered from 1 runtime process; 0 of 30 REPORT lines carried an Init Duration. race.py refuses a warm sample from a new process.

lanes.name: fcvm restore, UFFD
lanes.start: fcvm snapshot run --pid <serve> (memory paged in by a running fcvm snapshot serve)
lanes.config: 1 vCPU, 2048 MiB, rootless networking, port published on the host's loopback; one snapshot, restored by both fcvm lanes
lanes.check: 30 samples answered from 1 workload process and 1 kernel boot: every restore resumed the snapshot's own process (race.py refuses any other).

lanes.name: fcvm restore, memory file
lanes.start: fcvm snapshot run --snapshot <tag> (Firecracker maps the memory file; the wall's path)
lanes.config: 1 vCPU, 2048 MiB, rootless networking, port published on the host's loopback; one snapshot, restored by both fcvm lanes
lanes.check: 30 samples answered from 1 workload process and 1 kernel boot: every restore resumed the snapshot's own process (race.py refuses any other).

lanes.name: Lambda, cold start
lanes.start: HTTPS GET to the function URL, after an untimed code upload that retires the function's execution environments
lanes.config: provided.al2023, arm64, 2048 MB, function URL with IAM auth, BOOT_RACE_EXIT_AFTER_RESPONSE=1
lanes.check: 30 samples, each from a new runtime process; 30 of 30 REPORT lines carried an Init Duration. Before each sample race.py uploads new code so Lambda starts a new execution environment, and it refuses a sample whose REPORT line has no Init Duration.

lanes.name: ECS on EC2, warm host
lanes.start: RunTask on a running container instance, image already pulled
lanes.config: task 1 vCPU, 1536 MiB, ARM64, network mode host; container instance c8g.medium from al2023-ami-ecs-hvm-2023.0.20261031-kernel-6.1-arm64, image cached
lanes.check: 30 samples answered from 30 container processes on 1 kernel boot (the one container instance).

lanes.name: EC2 hibernate resume
lanes.start: StartInstances of an instance stopped with Hibernate=true
lanes.config: c8g.medium, gp3 8 GiB root, AMI made from al2023-ami-2023.12.20261102.0-kernel-6.1-arm64 with the workload as a systemd unit
lanes.check: 24 samples, 24 of them from the same process that answered before the instance hibernated, on 1 kernel boot: every start resumed the hibernated kernel. race.py refuses a resume that booted.

lanes.name: EC2 start of a stopped instance
lanes.config: c8g.medium, gp3 8 GiB root, AMI made from al2023-ami-2023.12.20261102.0-kernel-6.1-arm64 with the workload as a systemd unit
lanes.check: 30 samples answered from 30 processes and 30 kernel boots: every start booted.

lanes.name: EC2 launch from an AMI
lanes.start: RunInstances from an AMI with the workload installed
lanes.config: c8g.medium, gp3 8 GiB root, AMI made from al2023-ami-2023.12.20261102.0-kernel-6.1-arm64 with the workload as a systemd unit
lanes.check: 30 samples answered from 30 processes and 30 kernel boots: one per instance.

not_run.name: ECS on Fargate
not_run.why: The campaign's AWS configuration (ejc3/aws boot-race.tf) keeps this lane off. A Fargate task without a public IP pulls its image through ECR interface endpoints, which bill by the hour and change ECR DNS for the whole VPC, and they have no reviewed teardown yet.
